title: Minimum Impossible OR
summary: Given a 0-indexed integer array nums, find the smallest positive integer that cannot be expressed as the bitwise OR of any subsequence of nums.
statement: Given a 0-indexed integer array nums, find the smallest positive integer that cannot be expressed as the bitwise OR of any subsequence of nums.
constraints: Choose any subsequence, including multiple array elements, and OR its values.
Return the smallest positive integer that no subsequence can produce.
reference_solution:
def minimum_impossible_subsequence_or(nums):
    present=set(nums);value=1
    while value in present:value*=2
    return value
known_wrong_solutions:
def minimum_impossible_subsequence_or(nums):
    present=set(nums);value=1
    while value in present:value+=1
    return value
def minimum_impossible_subsequence_or(nums):
    present=set(nums[1:]);value=1
    while value in present:value*=2
    return value
hints: Any answer must itself be a power of two.
A power of two can appear as an OR only if some selected value contains that bit without higher bits; for the exact smallest missing bit, this requires that power itself.
Insert all values into a set and scan powers of two from one upward.
All smaller powers being present can OR-build every smaller positive value, while the first missing power cannot be built, proving minimality.
editorial: All smaller powers being present can OR-build every smaller positive value, while the first missing power cannot be built, proving minimality.

tests.explanation: Powers one and two are present and can form one through three, while four is impossible.
Power one is absent, so one is immediately impossible.
